name: Clear Cell Sarcoma of the Kidney

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for CCSK

criteria.description: Presence of uniform cells with clear cytoplasm arranged in nests or cords separated by delicate fibrovascular septa
Positive staining for vimentin and negative for WT1 and cytokeratin
Detection of BCOR internal tandem duplication or YWHAE-NUTM2 fusion gene by molecular testing
Large renal mass with heterogeneous enhancement on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with supportive immunohistochemistry and molecular genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of Wilms tumor and other pediatric renal neoplasms.

imaging: Large heterogeneous renal mass on ultrasound or CT scan
Possible lung nodules indicating metastases on chest imaging
Bone lesions visible on skeletal survey or MRI
other: Histopathology showing clear cells with fibrovascular septa
Immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin, negative for WT1 and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of triphasic histology (blastemal, epithelial, stromal components)
Typically presents in neonates and infants
Spindle cell morphology without clear cytoplasm
Distinct genetic alterations such as ETV6-NTRK3 fusion

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass in a young child
Evidence of metastatic spread to lungs or bones
